posts.heading: September 16, 2026
posts.text:
The day closed with 210 total feeder visits and 23 species recorded, a count significantly higher than the recent seven-day average. In the final hours, Northern Cardinals and Tufted Titmice provided the bulk of the remaining visual and acoustic activity as the light faded.

The last visual record of the day belonged to a Tufted Titmouse, spotted just 18 minutes before sunset. This bookended a long day of presence for the species, which had first arrived at 07:10. By 19:00, Blue Jays were still vocalizing with 19 detections, keeping the station active right up until the end of the day.

The day was both busier and more diverse than typical, with 790 total audio detections far exceeding the recent average of 357.

posts.heading: September 15, 2026
posts.text: Yesterday marked the busiest day in the past week, with 268 feeder visits and 21 species recorded, well above the seven-day average of 97 visits and 12 species. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees were the dominant visual presences, maintaining their status as regulars present every day this week. The station’s new seed feeder and treat bowl, installed over the past week, coincided with a significant increase in visitor diversity and frequency. A Black-capped Chickadee provided the station’s first confident visual record, joining a list that included a Common Gallinule, also a first visual for this location. The day closed with a final auditory detection of a Ruby-throated Hummingbird at 20:30. The high volume of detections, particularly from Carolina Wrens and Northern Cardinals, reflects the continued presence of the new microphone installed on September 13.

posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text: Yesterday registered 232 feeder visits and 16 species, a sharp increase from the recent weekly average of 63.6 visits and 10.0 species. The station’s activity ramped up following the installation of a new seed feeder on the morning of September 13, which replaced a unit that had been causing detection issues. This hardware change aligns with the steady rise in visual traffic observed over the last two days, culminating in yesterday’s high volume of Tufted Titmouse and Carolina Chickadee interactions.
